newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. military area of coverage in LatAm increases.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military area of coverage in LatAm increases.

text.p: The area of responsibility for U.S. military activities in Latin America will expand from Sunday to include the Caribbean and the Gulf of Mexico, the commander of U.S. forces in the region said on Friday

"Adding the Caribbean to the Southern Command's areas of responsibility will not affect or change the U.S. relationship with any of the island nations of the Caribbean," Gen. Wesley Clark told a news conference.
"Nor will our increased areas of responsibility mean any diminishing of our longtime relationships and focus on Central and South America," he said in a written statement.
The transfer, from the U.S. Atlantic Command, aligns the Caribbean and all of Latin America south of Mexico under one unified command, the Panama-based U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM).

It increases SOUTHCOM's area of responsibility to 32 nations and will also improve the integration of U.S. anti-narcotics efforts by giving one commander responsibility for both the source and transit zone, Clark said.

The transfer will not affect the move of SOUTHCOM headquarters to Miami in September. In accordance with bilateral treaties, the United States will withdraw all troops and turn over control of the Panama Canal by Dec. 31, 1999.
